newsitem.title: USA: Dlr closes mixed in US, sets 2-year high vs Swiss.
newsitem.headline: Dlr closes mixed in US, sets 2-year high vs Swiss.

text.p: The dollar ended down against the mark but rose modestly against the Swiss franc, which slumped against the German unit and dollar after Switzerland's economy showed more signs of distress.

Dollar/Swiss rose as the franc hit a 41-month low at 0.8577 per mark on speculation that Swiss interest rates, already among the world's lowest, are still stifling the economy and must be lowered again.
The mark/Swiss rise restrained dollar/mark, but dollar/yen was able to eke out modest gains, despite news of a wider Japanese trade surplus in November.
Dollar/mark ended at 1.5510/20, off from 1.5531/36 at the open, while dollar/yen rose to 113.65/70 from 113.55/60.

The dollar climbed to 1.3340 Swiss, its highest U.S. quote since early January 1995, before settling at 1.3285/95, up from 1.3275/85 at the open. Some dealers calculated a higher quote for dollar/Swiss in Asia trade on December 3.

Illustrating the heavy toll two years of subpar economic growth has taken on Switzerland, a report from semi-official credit watchdog Schweitzerischer Verband Creditreform on Wednesday said business bankruptcies rose 9.6 percent in the first 11 months of 1996 compared to last year.

"I think it is part and parcel of what's been weakening the Swiss," said David Gilmore, parnter at consulting firm Foreign Exchange Analytics. "You also have a central bank that has condoned depreciation and is committed to low interest rates."
The Swiss National Bank has loosened the credit reins aggressively this year after almost two years of consecutive quarter-to-quarter economic contractions.
So, with Swiss interest rates lower than those in any major country except Japan, the Swiss franc has been shunned by investors looking for higher yields.
Dollar/yen dipped to briefly to 113.27 in Tokyo after the Japanese Finance Ministry reported that Japan's trade surplus rose 0.2 percent as a weaker yen boosted auto exports.
"I would not be surprised if there was buying interest at 113 and that is probably what triggered some of the bounce," said Dennis Pettit, foreign exchange manager at Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan.

In contrast to its rally versus the Swiss, the mark fell against the pound, indirectly boosting the dollar, on expectations that German interest rates will eventually fall while British deposit rates might soon become more attractive.
Traders said the Bundesbank will probably keep rates steady at its bi-weekly meeting on Thursday after German M3 money supply growth slowed notably in November.
M3 expansion slowed to an annual rate of 8.0 percent in November, below October's 8.4 percent growth rate.
While slower money supply growth should please Bundesbank officials, M3 is still above their 4.0 to 7.0 percent target and most traders say the central bank is unlikely to ease yet.
"But you never know," said Ben Strauss, assistant vice president at Bank Julius Baer and Co. "Most of their rate moves catch the market by surprise."
The pound jumped after the U.K. announced that the number of unemployed Britons fell almost 96,000 in November.

"It seems to be pointing the way towards higher rates in the U.K., probably next year," said Dennis Pettit, foreign exchange manager at Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan. "That has caused sterling and sterling/mark to go bid and that is what brought dollar/mark up."
The pound rose to $1.6735/45 from $1.6715/25 at the open. The dollar rose to Canadian $1.3664/69 from C$1.3655/60. The Australian dollar fell to $0.7912/17 from $0.7920/25.
((-- Alden Bentley, 212 859 1667))
